content.value_statement: Generic data asset plans can miss sector rules, data ownership, buyer needs, and approval steps. This skill organizes industry selection, data assessment, compliance screening, commercialization scenarios, and repeatable delivery plans.
actual_capabilities: Compares candidate industries using data availability, policy support, customer budgets, organizational fit, and competition.
Profiles sector data by type, scale, format, update frequency, quality, and fragmentation.
Surfaces ownership, sensitivity, regulatory, and special-approval questions for specialist review.
Maps data value scenarios, likely buyers, budget sources, decision chains, and procurement approaches.
Outlines benchmark projects, delivery artifacts, quality checks, and replication plans for similar customers.
limitations: It does not provide legal, regulatory, accounting, valuation, or investment advice.
Current laws, approvals, and jurisdiction-specific obligations require review by qualified local specialists.
The package references internal cases and materials that are not included in the four supplied files.
Recommendations depend on accurate information about the organization, data rights, jurisdiction, and intended use.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a Data-Rich Sector
use_cases.description: Compare candidate industries and select one or two sectors for focused data asset development.

use_cases.title: Screen a Sector Data Project
use_cases.description: Identify data traits, ownership questions, sensitive data, regulations, approvals, and evidence gaps before design.

use_cases.title: Replicate a Benchmark Project
use_cases.description: Turn one delivery into reusable materials, validation criteria, buyer messaging, and a rollout sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Describe an Industry Data Opportunity
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the data opportunity in [industry]. List data types, producers, update frequency, quality concerns, and value scenarios. State your assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Compliance Screening Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [industry] data project in [jurisdiction]. Identify sensitive data, ownership questions, sector rules, approvals, evidence gaps, and required specialist reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Map Scenarios and Buyers
prompt_templates.prompt: For [data assets], rank commercial scenarios by value and feasibility. For each scenario, describe buyers, budget owners, decision makers, procurement routes, and proof requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Benchmark and Replication Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a benchmark project for [industry and client]. Include phases, inputs, controls, deliverables, acceptance criteria, dependencies, risks, and a replication plan.

output_examples.input: Assess whether a hospital imaging dataset is ready for commercialization.
output: Readiness: conditional, pending ownership, patient authorization, de-identification, and sector approval review.
Priority evidence: data inventory, notices, consent records, rights agreements, security controls, and permitted-use records.
Next step: obtain specialist review before selecting a buyer or valuation approach.

output_examples.input: Turn a charging-network data project into a replication plan.
output: Standardize the data inventory, metrics, compliance checks, buyer profile, and acceptance criteria.
Separate reusable methods from client-specific contracts, infrastructure, permissions, and financial assumptions.
Validate the package with a second customer before wider rollout.

best_practices: Provide the industry, jurisdiction, data sources, rights, intended use, and available evidence.
Treat compliance and ownership as decision gates before valuation or commercialization.
Validate recommendations with current regulations, primary evidence, and qualified sector specialists.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse one generic data asset plan across industries with different regulatory obligations.
Do not present scenario assumptions, estimated values, or cited internal cases as verified facts.
Do not start commercialization while ownership, consent, approval, or data-quality questions remain unresolved.

faq.question: Which industries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for healthcare, agriculture, energy, education, carbon, trade finance, commodities, entertainment, consumer data, and related sectors.

faq.question: Can it choose the best industry for my organization?
faq.answer: It can structure and score the decision. Final selection needs verified resources, market evidence, budgets, competition, and organizational priorities.

faq.question: Does it provide legal or regulatory approval?
faq.answer: No. It identifies review areas and evidence gaps. Qualified specialists and authorities must confirm requirements.

faq.question: Can it value a dataset?
faq.answer: It can prepare industry context and value scenarios. Defensible valuation requires verified financial evidence, suitable methods, and qualified professionals.

faq.question: Does the package include the cited internal cases?
faq.answer: No. The knowledge base refers to internal materials, but the underlying documents and datasets are not included.

faq.question: What information produces the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the industry, jurisdiction, data inventory, ownership evidence, collection basis, intended uses, buyer hypotheses, and known regulatory constraints.
